questions.q: What did David ask Yahweh, and what was the reply?
questions.a: David asked if he should go up to one of the cities of Judah, and Yahweh told him to go up.

questions.q: When David inquired further, to which city did Yahweh tell David to go?
questions.a: Yahweh told David to go to Hebron.

questions.q: Who went up with David to Hebron?
questions.a: David went up to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, and all his men and their families.

questions.q: What did the men of Judah do when they came to David?
questions.a: The men of Judah came and anointed David as king over the house of Judah.

questions.q: What did Abner do with Ishbosheth, the son of Saul?
questions.a: Abner took Ishbosheth to Mahanaim and made him king of all the territory that would later be the northern kingdom of Israel.
Abner was the son of Ner and the commander of Saul’s army.

questions.q: How long was David king in Hebron over the house of Judah?
questions.a: David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah for seven years and six months.

questions.q: Where did Joab’s men and Abner’s men meet?
questions.a: They met near the large pool of Gibeon, staying on opposite sides of the pool.

questions.q: How many young men fought before Joab and Abner?
questions.a: Twelve men from Benjamin for Ishbosheth and twelve men from David’s soldiers fought.

questions.q: Who won the battle that day?
questions.a: The soldiers of David defeated Abner and the soldiers from the other tribes of Israel.

questions.q: Which son of Zeruiah pursued Abner?
How did Abner try to convince Asahel to stop pursuing him?
questions.a: Abner warned Asahel that if he had to strike him down, he could never again have a peaceful relationship with Asahel’s brother Joab.

questions.q: What happened to Asahel when he refused to stop pursuing Abner?
questions.a: Abner struck him in the stomach with the butt end of his spear, and the spear went right through his stomach and came out of his back, so Asahel fell and died there.

questions.q: To what location did Joab and Abishai pursue Abner?
questions.a: Joab and Abishai pursued Abner to the hill of Ammah, which is near Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.

questions.q: What did Abner say to stop Joab from pursuing him?
questions.a: Abner called out to Joab that they should not continue this deadly battle any longer. He told Joab to realize that if they continue fighting, many people will suffer great harm. He said that they are all Israelites, and asked Joab to please tell his soldiers right now to stop chasing Abner and his soldiers.

questions.q: Where did Abner and his men travel?
questions.a: Abner and his men marched back to Mahanaim.

questions.q: Where did Joab and his men travel?
questions.a: Joab and his men traveled to Hebron to bury Asahel’s body in the tomb of his father at Bethlehem. Then they marched all night, going back to Hebron, their home.

commentary.text: Abner makes Ishbosheth king Battle between Abner's men and those of Joab.

Verses 1–7 After the death of Saul, many went to David at Ziklag, 1Ch 12:22, but he trusted in God who promised him the kingdom, to give it in his own time and manner. Yet assurance of hope in God's promise, will quicken pious endeavours. If I be chosen to the crown of life, it does not follow, Then I will do nothing; but, Then I will do all that God directs me. This good use David made of his election, and so will all whom God has chosen. In all our journeys and removes, it is comfortable to see God going before us; and we may do so, if by faith and prayer we set Him before us. God, according to the promise, directed David's path. David rose gradually: thus the kingdom of the Messiah, the Son of David, is set up by degrees; he is Lord of all, but we see not yet all things put under him.

The nation in general refused David. By this the Lord trained up his servant for future honour and usefulness; and the tendency of true godliness was shown in his behaviour while passing through various difficulties. David was herein a type of Christ, whom Israel would not submit to, though anointed of the Father to be a Prince and a Saviour to them. Abner meant, Let the young men fight before us, when he said, Let them play before us: fools thus make a mock at sin. But he is unworthy the name of a man, that can thus trifle with human blood.
Death often comes by ways we least suspect. We are often betrayed by the accomplishments we are proud of! Asahel's swiftness, which he presumed so much upon, did him no service, but hastened his end.

Abner appeals to Joab concerning the miserable consequences of a civil war. Those who make light of such unnatural contests, will find that they are bitterness to all concerned. How easy it is for men to use reason, when it makes for them, who would not use it, if it made against them! See how the issue of things alter men's minds! The same thing which looked pleasant in the morning, at night looked dismal. Those who are most forward to enter into contention, will repent before they have done with it, and had better leave it off before it be meddled with, as Solomon advises. This is true of every sin, oh that men would consider it in time, that it will be bitterness in the latter end! Asahel's funeral is here mentioned. Distinctions are made between the dust of some and that of others; but in the resurrection no difference will be made, but between the godly and ungodly, which will remain for ever.
